--- title: "Debugging with reprex() and browser()" description: "" author: - Etienne Bacher - Niklas Hohmann date: "2026-11-16" brand: _brand/_brand.yml format: revealjs: output-file: index-slides.html toc: false css: style/template.css slide-number: c/t include-in-header: style/header.html include-after-body: style/footer.html execute: echo: true eval: false warning: false message: false freeze: auto editor: markdown: wrap: 72 --- ## Objectives
- Learn the essential steps to debug R code . . . - Create a small reproducible example with `reprex` . . . - Use `browser()` and breakpoints ## A failing script From the ["Latitudinal trends in Phanerozoic reefs"](https://palaeoverse.palaeoverse.org/articles/phanerozoic-reefs.html) vignette: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(palaeoverse) data(reefs) reef_counts <- group_apply(occdf = reefs, group = "interval", fun = nrow) reefs <- look_up(occdf = reefs, early_interval = "interval", late_interval = "interval", int_key = interval_key) reefs <- subset(reefs, interval_max_ma <= 541) bins <- time_bins(interval = "Phanerozoic", rank = "stage") bin_time(occdf = reefs, bins = bins, method = "mid") ``` ::: ``` #> Error in `[.data.frame`: #> ! undefined columns selected ``` ## A failing script
Using `traceback()` to see the chain of errors: ``` > traceback() 4: stop("undefined columns selected") 3: `[.data.frame`(occdf, , max_ma, drop = TRUE) 2: occdf[, max_ma, drop = TRUE] 1: bin_time(occdf = reefs, bins = bins, method = "mid") at #1 ``` . . .
The root cause is not very clear. # Reducing the problem ## Minimal reproducible example
- Longer code = more potential causes . . . - First: build a **repr**oducible **ex**ample, aka a *reprex* . . . - Two steps: 1. reduce the data 1. reduce the code ## Reduce the data
Smaller data: - runs faster - makes outputs easier to compare . . . Our dataset has thousands of rows and 14 columns: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(palaeoverse) dim(reefs) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 4363 14 ``` ::: ::: ## Reduce the data Keep only the first 6 rows: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="1"} reefs2 <- head(reefs) reef_counts <- group_apply(occdf = reefs2, group = "interval", fun = nrow) reefs2 <- look_up(occdf = reefs2, early_interval = "interval", late_interval = "interval", int_key = interval_key) reefs2 <- subset(reefs2, interval_max_ma <= 541) bins <- time_bins(interval = "Phanerozoic", rank = "stage") bin_time(occdf = reefs2, bins = bins, method = "mid") ``` ::: ``` #> Error in `[.data.frame`: #> ! undefined columns selected ``` ## Reduce the data
Keep 1 row and 5 columns: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="1-2"} reefs2 <- head(reefs, n = 1) reefs2 <- reefs2[, 1:5] reef_counts <- group_apply(occdf = reefs2, group = "interval", fun = nrow) ``` ::: ``` Error in `group_apply()`: ! Supplied `group` is not a named column in `occdf` ``` ## Reduce the data Keep 1 row and 6 columns: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="1-2"} reefs2 <- head(reefs, n = 1) reefs2 <- reefs2[, 1:6] reef_counts <- group_apply(occdf = reefs2, group = "interval", fun = nrow) reefs2 <- look_up(occdf = reefs2, early_interval = "interval", late_interval = "interval", int_key = interval_key) reefs2 <- subset(reefs2, interval_max_ma <= 541) bins <- time_bins(interval = "Phanerozoic", rank = "stage") bin_time(occdf = reefs2, bins = bins, method = "mid") ``` ::: ``` #> Error in `[.data.frame`: #> ! undefined columns selected ``` ## Reduce the code Remove as much code as possible to limit potential causes. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|4|9"} reefs2 <- head(reefs, n = 1) reefs2 <- reefs2[, 1:6] reef_counts <- group_apply(occdf = reefs2, group = "interval", fun = nrow) reefs2 <- look_up(occdf = reefs2, early_interval = "interval", late_interval = "interval", int_key = interval_key) reefs2 <- subset(reefs2, interval_max_ma <= 541) bins <- time_bins(interval = "Phanerozoic", rank = "stage") bin_time(occdf = reefs2, bins = bins, method = "mid") ``` ::: ## Reduce the code
- `reef_counts` is never used: remove it . . . - Does `subset()` do anything with one row? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} identical(reefs2, subset(reefs2, interval_max_ma <= 541)) #> [1] TRUE ``` ::: . . . - No: remove it too ## Reduce the code
What we have now: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} reefs2 <- head(reefs, n = 1) reefs2 <- reefs2[, 1:6] reefs2 <- look_up(occdf = reefs2, early_interval = "interval", late_interval = "interval", int_key = interval_key) bins <- time_bins(interval = "Phanerozoic", rank = "stage") bin_time(occdf = reefs2, bins = bins, method = "mid") ``` ::: . . . Two function calls removed, but still no clear cause. ## Next step

Stuck? Ask for help (GitHub, StackOverflow, colleagues).
. . . But before that... # Is your reprex really a reprex? ## Clean the environment
Our session may contain objects and options unrelated to the problem. . . .
They can interact with our code. . . .
Restarting R works, but is easy to forget. ## `reprex()`
[`reprex::reprex()`](https://reprex.tidyverse.org/) runs code in a separate, clean R session. . . .
- Errors if the code isn't self-contained . . . - If it runs in `reprex()`, others can reproduce it ## `reprex()` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} reprex::reprex({ reefs2 <- head(reefs, n = 1) reefs2 <- reefs2[, 1:6] reefs2 <- look_up(occdf = reefs2, early_interval = "interval", late_interval = "interval", int_key = interval_key) bins <- time_bins(interval = "Phanerozoic", rank = "stage") bin_time(occdf = reefs2, bins = bins, method = "mid") }) ``` ::: . . . ``` reefs2 <- head(reefs, n = 1) #> Error: #> ! object 'reefs' not found ``` ## `reprex()` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="2-3"} reprex::reprex({ library(palaeoverse) data(reefs) reefs2 <- head(reefs, n = 1) reefs2 <- reefs2[, 1:6] reefs2 <- look_up(occdf = reefs2, early_interval = "interval", late_interval = "interval", int_key = interval_key) bins <- time_bins(interval = "Phanerozoic", rank = "stage") bin_time(occdf = reefs2, bins = bins, method = "mid") }) ``` ::: . . . ``` bin_time(occdf = reefs2, bins = bins, method = "mid") #> Error in `[.data.frame`: #> ! undefined columns selected ``` ## `reprex()`
Good practice: add session info with `session_info = TRUE`. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="4"} reprex::reprex({ library(palaeoverse) ... }, session_info = TRUE) ``` ::: . . .
Reducing the problem is key, and often reveals the bug by itself. # Debugging a function ## Debugging a function
A function runs a whole block of code and only shows the final error. . . .
One solution: add `print()` statements. . . .
Better: `browser()` pauses execution *inside* the function. ## Example
Based on [issue #280](https://github.com/palaeoverse/palaeoverse/issues/280) in `palaeoverse` (now fixed): ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(palaeoverse) occdf <- reefs[1:5, ] bin_space(occdf = occdf, spacing = 1000, sub_grid = 250, return = TRUE) ``` ::: ``` Error in `bin_space()`: ! object 'secondary' not found ``` . . .
`bin_space()` is a long function: where does it fail? ## `browser()`
Add `browser()` at the top, reload the function, and rerun the code: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="4"} function (occdf, lng = "lng", lat = "lat", spacing = 100, sub_grid = NULL, return = FALSE, plot = FALSE) { browser() if (!is.data.frame(occdf)) { stop("occdf should be of class dataframe") } [ MANUALLY TRUNCATED ] } ``` ::: ## `browser()`
Execution stops at `browser()`: - We have access to the function environment. . . . - Press "Enter" to run the next statement. . . . - Only the path actually taken is executed (e.g. no `if (FALSE)`). . . . - Press "Esc" or run `Q` to exit. ## `browser()`
Step through until the code fails: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} occdf <- list(occdf, grid, base_grid, primary, secondary) ``` ::: . . .
Tip: move `browser()` past lines that are irrelevant. ## Breakpoints
Built into IDEs like RStudio or Positron. . . .
Click left of a line number to add one. . . .
Same as `browser()`, without modifying the code. ## Breakpoints
![](breakpoint_screenshot.png){fig-alt="A screenshot of RStudio. The left hand side shows the editor with the source code of `bin_space()`. On the left of the line number, a circle filled in red indicates the location of the breakpoint."} # Conclusion ## Conclusion
- Reduce the data and the code . . . - Check your reprex with `reprex()` . . . - Inspect functions with `browser()` and breakpoints . . .
Good debugging helps you fix your code and improves bug reports.

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
